author: TEDx Talks
description:
This husband-and-wife research team discusses how a little bit of math can help you with medical decisions and, along the way, introduces cutting-edge transplant advances. Dr. Sommer Gentry is a Professor in the Department of Surgery at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. She co-directs the Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (C-STAR) at NYU Langone Health.

Dr. Dorry Segev is a Professor in the Departments of Surgery and Population Health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. He is also the Vice Chair of the Department of Surgery and Surgical Sciences and he co-directs the Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (C-STAR) at NYU Langone Health.

title: How math can help with health decisions | Sommer Gentry & Dorry Segev | TEDxNYU Langone Health

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The present eclipses the past in so much of our modern world. We are the lesser for it. Our stories and those handed down to us have the power to transcend the prevailing NOW. 

Recent grandparenthood and a dedication of Thursdays to looking after the grandchildren led me to reflect on the role of the grandparent. It is so much more than entertaining the children and 'giving them back at the end of the day'. Grandparenthood gives the privilege of time to build a legacy: a legacy, beyond the material, of a familial and cultural kind. We communicate our legacy in our stories which confirm our humanity. Such secure roots are doubly important in a technological age of hyper immediacy, self-absorption and shortening attention spans. We should champion the long view and ask ourselves: what has the past shared with me? What story will I embody for the future? Born in Brighton, Julian feels most naturally at home by the sea. He has taught English in the Portsmouth and Gosport area for the gre
title: The Power Of Legacy: What Will Your Story Be? | Julian Elphick-Smith | TEDxGosport

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when personal passion meets purpose? This talk traces the journey of how one person's ideas and creativity can spark something far bigger than themselves, inspiring others, mobilizing communities, and eventually shaping a collective movement or culture.

Drawing from a personal journey across law, brand strategy, hospitality, and content creation, this talk unpacks how a single conviction can grow into a system that connects people and creates real, lasting impact. It's a story of how combining law, media, and culture can build bridges between disciplines and, more importantly, between people, creating a ripple effect that reaches far beyond where it started.

If you've ever wondered how individual drive turns into community-driven change, this talk offers a firsthand look at what that process actually looks like. Bamidele Olamilekan is a renowned entertainment lawyer, prolific author, and dynamic speaker. As the Principal Partner at Lekan Bamidele & Co., he has carved a
title: Individual spark to collective fire | Olamilekan Bamidele (King Pexxie) | TEDxLead City University

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lucrezia reflects on the subtle strength of self-belief, guiding us through how internal conviction can carry us through life's loudest doubts.
 Lucrezia has faced challenges through her studies and these moments led her to focus on this topic for her TED talk. The 'power of yet' resonated with her after researching ways to calmly revisit errors and areas to improve. She hopes to inspire others! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The power of yet | Lucrezia M | TEDxCanadian School Milan

author: TEDx Talks
description:
There's a difference between what we build alone and what we build together. Individual effort adds, but collaboration multiplies. This talk explores that shift, how bringing people, ideas, and disciplines together doesn't just add value, it raises it exponentially.

Through personal experience across law, media, and culture, this talk breaks down how collaboration turns isolated effort into collective momentum, and how the right connections can take an idea from a single spark to a system that carries far more than one person ever could alone.

It's a case for why "we" will always outperform "I," and what it actually takes to build something raised to that power. Kamsi Asuzu-Obumselu is a strategist, brand storyteller, and creative leader passionate
about designing spaces of meaning for young people to grow, lead, and create impact.
She currently serves as the CEO and Executive Director of Limitless Club, a fast-growing
movement equipping young people with the mindsets, skills, and c
title: The surprising power of ‘we' | Kamsi Asuzu- Obumselu | TEDxLead City University

author: TEDx Talks
description: Many people facing a cancer diagnosis experience loneliness and social isolation.  In addition to worsening quality of life, such experiences are associated with shorter survival.  Few realize they hold a life-changing healing power through regular outreach in the form of audio and written communication.  We discuss that intentional, small-form efforts for connection can be rewarding to both allies of persons with cancer and the patients themselves, and can be achieved in as little as seconds a day.  Complemented with usual therapies provided by doctors, communities can work together to improve the lives of millions of people who seek more and better days during their cancer journey.  Dr. Arif Kamal is the inaugural chief patient officer for the American Cancer Society, a practicing oncologist and palliative care physician in North Carolina, and an associate professor of medicine and population health at the Duke University School of Medicine. He has published more than 225 peer-revie
title: How to support loved ones with cancer | Dr.  Arif Kamal | TEDxRaleigh

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Vivimos rodeados de información, estímulos y ruido. Estamos tan acostumbrados a llenar cada silencio que hemos dejado de preguntarnos qué pasa cuando simplemente estamos con nosotros mismos.

Alejandro Tapia de Jesús nos invita a reflexionar sobre cómo construimos nuestra realidad, cómo interpretamos lo que nos sucede y cuánto de lo que somos está realmente en nuestras manos.

A través de ejercicios, una ilusión óptica, meditación e imaginación, la charla propone volver a lo esencial: reconocer lo que pensamos, sentimos y somos. En un mundo donde las redes sociales, las etiquetas y la tecnología ocupan cada vez más espacio en nuestra vida, la invitación es a recuperar nuestra atención, nuestra identidad y nuestra capacidad de imaginar.

Porque nuestra grandeza no está solamente en cuánto podemos brillar, sino en cuánto podemos iluminar a los demás. Keep looking at the stars. One day you will be there. Alejandro Tapia de Jesús, es Doctor en Investigación Psicológica por la Universidad
title: Con-Ciencia: ¿Quién soy? | Alejandro Tapia de Jesús | TEDxUniversidad Iberoamericana CDMX

author: TEDx Talks
description: A journey through growing up, finding purpose, and learning that maybe the point isn’t to save the world but to help people believe it can be different. A story about Korle Lagoon, impossible things, and the power of asking: why not? Katia Osei, also known as Katya the Destroyer, is a Ghanaian engineer, researcher, and storyteller working to democratize the "-isms" and "-ologies" long reserved for the privileged few. After studying bioengineering at Harvard University, she returned to Ghana's coastline, a historic site where many of the stories that shaped today's unequal world were first told. Her work spans genetic engineering to community ecology, bridging conventional academia and citizen scence. Katia believes that the world as we know it was first spoken into being and that new stories, told from this same coast, can help unbuild it into something fairer. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn m
title: Hey Everyone. I’m Katya the Destroyer | Katya Osei | TEDxAccra

Partnership isn't a business strategy Africa's industrialists adopted; it is a stewardship tradition they inherited and scaled. The same logic that built Kwahu trading networks built Dangote's empire. If we want the next generation of African industrial giants, we have to stop celebrating solo founders and start deliberately building and teaching symbiosis. Emmanuel Osei Ntim leads FON Packaging Ventures, one of
Ghana's leading corrugated carton manufacturers, and founded
EON Investments. A proud Kwahu and the eldest of four brothers,
he grew up inside the family business his parents built from a
trading shop in Tudu, on the factory floor from the age of twelve.
Educated at Ghana International School and Bryant University in
Rhode Island, he was back at work in Accra within 48 hours of
graduating. Under his leadership, the company grew from an internal
supply solution into a manufacturer serving Nestlé, Wilmar and
Olam. Today he writes and speaks on African industrialization and
secon
title: What Africa's industrialists taught me | Emmanuel Osei Ntim | TEDxAccra

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores the counterfactual question of what would have happened if large-scale colonisation had not occurred in the region which we now call the United States of America. This talk discusses how modern nations and borders are not inevitable, and are influenced by historical actions, political decisions, and geography.  Holly Fitzpatrick is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Politics, Economics and Religious Studies. She hopes to study International Relations at university. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What If the US Wasn't Colonised? | Holly Fitzpatrick | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square

description: We all have called the government a number of colourful names at some point and most people mainly seem to focus on the negative aspects of a politicians career, painting most in a bad light. However, we largely do not apply the same attitudes to companies that arguably have the same influence and power as governments. So what if companies were running our governments. Would we be better off?  Jemima Gray is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Politics, English and History of Art. She hopes to study Politics and International Relations at university and has a particular interest in how governments define their international identity and their subsequent influence in global politics This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. author: TEDx Talks
description: What if one of the most intelligent conversations on Earth has been happening underwater this whole time? This talk explores how artificial intelligence is being used to analyse sperm whale vocalisations, uncovering patterns that challenge the way we think about language, intelligence, and consciousness itself. Blending marine biology, AI, and philosophy, it asks a deeper question: if another species may possess a complex form of communication, what does that force us to reconsider about humanity’s place in the natural world? Alice Chavarot is a student in the Lower Sixth studying English Literature, Mathematics, Biology, and Spanish. She hopes to study Biology at University and is particularly interested in animal sciences. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What if we could speak to animals? | Alice Chavarot | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Violeta Alvarez  explores the idea that energy may be the hidden foundation beneath everything we value. While economies are usually understood through money, markets, and finance, this talk reframes civilisation through a more fundamental lens: the ability to harness, transfer, and utilise energy.

Blending ideas from physics, engineering, and economics, the talk examines whether economic growth is ultimately a reflection of energy use, and what that means for the future of global development. By questioning how value is created in the first place, this talk challenges the audience to rethink the systems that underpin modern life. Violeta Alvarez is a driven 17 year old student who enjoys using an interdisciplinary approach to understand the world around her. She is studying Physics, Economics and Maths with aims to study Mechanical Engineering at University. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local
title: If energy was the only currency | Violeta Alvarez Carcedo | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square

author: TEDx Talks
description: We often feel fear on different occasions such as within our journey of growing up, or even when missing out on certain occasions. It is part of our identity and is what makes us, us . The decisions we make, the actions we take, they are all done in fear. So take it away, take all of the fear away and what are we left with. Is it good or bad?  Starla DeLucy McKeeve is a student in lower sixth studying psychology, politics, and drama. She hopes to study marketing at Edinburgh university. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What if fear never existed? | Starla DeLucy McKeeve | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square

description:
La charla aborda la importancia de la perseverancia, la disciplina y la determinación para alcanzar los objetivos personales y profesionales. Como ejemplo, se presenta la experiencia de Daniel, quien desde temprana edad tuvo el sueño de convertirse en piloto de automovilismo, participar en competencias y tener presencia en televisión. A pesar de que sus inicios en el ámbito profesional no fueron los esperados, mantuvo firme su propósito y continuó trabajando para alcanzar su meta. Después de eso fue piloto durante 10 años, logró consolidarse como corredor profesional.

Se destaca la importancia de conocer y familiarizarse con estas nuevas herramientas tecnológicas, aprovechando sus beneficios para complementar nuestros conocimientos, facilitar el aprendizaje y adquirir nuevas habilidades. Sin embargo, también se enfatiza la necesidad de no generar una dependencia excesiva de la intel
title: Liderazgo | Daniel Ordaz Cortés | TEDxUMAE34

author: TEDx Talks
description:
MISTER TWO FIVE is a 21-year-old Malaysian alternative hip-hop artist, songwriter and producer. Rooted in hip-hop and shaped by jazz, neo-soul and R&B, his work pairs gritty production with writing on self-worth, ambition and identity. He is part of the Kuala Lumpur creative collective Out The Middle and released his debut album, STATE OF THE ART, in 2025.

You Will Never Be Me comes out of growing up in Malaysia, choosing an unconventional creative path, and the pressure to become someone the world finds easier to understand. 

The piece turns on a single tension: the parts of yourself that make you feel out of place may be the parts worth holding onto, and the cost of belonging is usually paid in pieces of who you were. MISTER TWO FIVE is a 21-year-old artist crafting a sound rooted in hip-hop and shaped by jazz, neo-soul, and R&B. His music thrives on tension: gritty, distorted drums and basslines cutting against lush chords on keys and guitar. This contrast is matched by thoughtfu
title: You Will Never Be Me | MISTERTWOFIVE | Amaresh Raam Murali | TEDxAsia Pacific U

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In his talk, Erwan Blanc-Paques talks about a small moment on a school bus that made him question what it really means to be American. By sharing his experience of moving from a small town in the French Alps to San Francisco, Erwan highlights how hard it was to learn a new language, culture, and way of life. After many years in the United States, Erwan explains that he still feels like he doesn’t fully fit in. But instead of seeing this as just his problem, he realizes that this feeling is actually something many people in America share, because the country is made up of immigrants from different times and places. In the end, Erwan’s talk shows that no one ever fully becomes “American,” and that we are all still learning, growing, and finding our place.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. A junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory High School in San Francisco, Erwan Blanc-Paques helps lead the Entrep
title: We’re all still arriving | Erwan Blanc-Paques | TEDxSHC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In cities where mosquitoes are becoming increasingly difficult to control, Tim Liu sees more than a public health problem — he sees a warning about our relationship with nature. With experience in wildlife field observation and expeditions, as well as a background in finance, he now brings systems thinking, data analysis, and ecological observation into ecological restoration, biodiversity, and nature education. His work explores a deceptively simple question: what happens when we stop trying to control nature, and instead create space for other forms of life to return? 1、Founder of Gaia Wish | Practitioner in Ecological Restoration and Biodiversity Conservation
2、Ecology Lecturer | Advocate for Nature Education
3、Participated in Discovery and RGS nature documentary and field expedition projects This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Mosquitoes, Nuts, and Seeds | Tim Liu | TEDxWukang Rd

description: This talk was presented in TEDxNICYouth 2026 with the theme of the event being "The Ripple Effect" Dennis Wei Lie Ching sees himself as a bridge-builder between industries, cultures, and generations. A citizen of Taiwan, he operates in the high-stakes world of global manufacturing across Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Taiwan. Beyond his professional leadership, he is also a competitive Hyrox athlete who believes that the discipline developed in the gym mirrors the discipline required in the office, laboratory, and manufacturing floor. He brings these perspectives not only as a global executive, but also as a father and community member, emphasizing how the smallest motions can create the largest waves and lasting impact. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: From the Product development War room to the dining table | Dennis Ching | TEDxNIC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores the nature of risk and what makes certain risks worth taking. Erin draws on personal experiences from the enormous risk of moving to a different country with no safety net to the incredibly low risk activity of fishing. The talk delves into psychological research and spiritual reflection, and culminates in an invitation to reconsider how to embrace uncertainty, participation, and belief. The philosophical core of Erin's talk is the idea that risk is really just the acknowledgment that we are participating in this life, not orchestrating it.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Erin Baldanzi is the Theology Department Chair, instructor of theology, and Fishing Club moderator at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory in San Francisco. In her free time, she not only enjoys fishing, but almost anything outdoors, including hiking, paddle boarding, and simple walks with her dog. This talk was giv
title: Risk & Reward: Life’s Best Bets | Erin Baldanzi | TEDxSHC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
After a bullying incident in her freshman year of high school, Eva Richey realized how damaging people's misconceptions about autism could be. Eva explains how the misconception that autism functions more like a mental illness than a disorder couldn't be farther from the truth, as she highlights how she lives her life as a person on the autism spectrum. In her talk, Eva dives into what a "disorder" really is, and how autism is only a problem if society makes it one.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Eva is a junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory High School in San Francisco, where she regularly participates in Theatre productions, Chamber Choir, and the Jewish Heritage Club. Eva hopes to become an actress one day, but more than that, she wants to become a symbol for autistic success in life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a loca
title: ASD: Autism’s Societal Disorder | Eva Richey | TEDxSHC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ellen’s talk breaks down the manipulative culture of the modern fast fashion industry and how social media has worked side by side with it to promote fast, cheap trends, taking away our individuality. She analyzes the complex system and how cheap labor, environmental factors, and scrolling culture has led us to a worldwide crisis. She reflects upon her own personal experience with thrifting, on how buying second hand clothing has not only allowed her to live a more sustainable lifestyle, but a way to find her true identity.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Ellen Dale is a junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral in San Francisco. The 2026-27 Student Body President, Ellen brought the idea of a dress code apparel thrift store to promote sustainability within her school community. She is a leader of Go Big Green, the school spirit group, and devotes countless hours to ballet outside of school. In Ellen's free ti
title: Something Once Loved | Ellen Dale | TEDxSHC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Alyssa‘s talk is a reflection on her Math Team experience, which sparked her interest in understanding girls‘ confidence in math and science. She presents research showing that gender and socioeconomic gaps in STEM share similar root causes, such as limited early exposure, lack of encouragement, stereotypes, and a shortage of role models. Drawing from her work as a peer tutor and student teacher, Alyssa offers practical ways we can begin to close these gaps.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Alyssa Huang is a junior at the Branson School in Ross, California, who founded AspireED, a student-led organization committed to expanding access to STEM education. Alyssa’s interests include chemistry, sustainability, basketball, photography, and making French pastries. author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often overlook the importance of life’s small moments, focusing instead on major milestones and achievements. From something as seemingly insignificant as a fruit fly to the quiet, fleeting moments spent with our grandparents, Francesca highlights how these details are easy to dismiss. Yet many fail to recognize just how meaningful and impactful these small things truly are.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Francesca Rinaudo is a junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory High School in San Francisco, where she is part of the Emerald, the school newspaper; president of Advocacy and Action; California Scholarship Federation; and is also an ambassador for Irish for A Day, her school’s shadow program. In her free time, she likes to play soccer, tennis and go thrifting with friends. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Humans are wired for connection, with relations being an intrinsic part of human life and wellbeing. In her talk, Anska Hilash explores the idea that true friends, free of expectations, help us to reflect and reveal who we are, creating who we know as our authentic selves. 
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.
 Anska Hilash is a junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory, where she serves as an Opinion Editor of the Emerald, the school newspaper, and is involved in Speech and Debate, Model UN, and SHC Live. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At 16 years old, Simone Myers made a decision that most teenagers would consider unthinkable: she voluntarily gave up her phone for an entire year. Simone thought going a year without a phone meant giving something up. Instead, she got her life back. In her talk, Simone describes how removing her phone revealed how important key presence actually is for real friendships, self-awareness, and emotional maturity. She argues that these are all factors that only come from staying inside moments we usually escape with our phones.
This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Simone Myers is a junior at Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory High School in San Francisco, where she competes on both the Varsity Soccer and Lacrosse teams. Driven by a deep curiosity about how people connect and grow, Simone has dedicated herself to working with children, tutoring youth who are second-language learners, and serving as a camp coun
title: Presence Is Power | Simone Myers | TEDxSHC Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Africa’s participation in the global economy has historically followed a familiar pattern: the continent exports raw materials while importing the higher-value products created from them.  

Artificial intelligence depends on data, languages, cultural knowledge, research, human experience and feedback. Africa possesses these essential resources, yet much of the infrastructure that transforms them into intelligent products—including computing systems, models, platforms and intellectual property—is controlled elsewhere. As AI commoditises cognitive capabilities, Africa could simultaneously become a supplier of knowledge and a recurring purchaser of the intelligence produced from it.

The argument is not against adopting global AI. Rather, it challenges Africa to reconsider its position within the emerging intelligence value chain. Prof. Isaac Wiafe is a Professor of Information Technology at the University of Ghana and the Founder and Lead of the Human–Computer Interaction Lab, at the D
title: Will Africa Export Knowledge and Import Intelligence? | Isaac Wiafe | TEDxAccra

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if making life easier isn’t always the same as making life better?

We spend much of our lives trying to remove friction—for ourselves, for the people we love, and for the people we lead. But some of the experiences we’re quickest to smooth away may be doing something important.

Drawing from her own life, psychology, and nearly two decades spent designing products to reduce friction, Rachael Tachie-Menson explores what difficulty can teach us about our own capability and asks us to reconsider our instinct to make every path easier.
 Rachael Tachie-Menson is a product leader, strategist and ecosystem architect who has spent nearly two decades building products and businesses at the intersection of technology, people and growth.
Her career spans some of the world’s most influential technology companies, including Meta, Amazon, LinkedIn, Yahoo and WeWork, as well as startups across North America and Africa. She has built and scaled products from zero to one and led product portfoli
title: A life without friction | Rachael Tachie-Menson | TEDxAccra
